newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: North Korea seen hinting acceptance of defection.
newsitem.headline: North Korea seen hinting acceptance of defection.

text.p: North Korea has suggested it may accept the defection of a top Pyongyang official taking refuge in the South Korean embassy in China by saying it would dismiss him if he sought asylum, Seoul officials said on Tuesday.

"It is certain North Korea is changing its attitude," said Kim Kyung-woong, a senior official at the state South-North Dialogue Office. North Korea had maintained that Seoul kidnapped Hwang Jang-yop, ranked 24th in Pyongyang's hierarchy.
"North Korea appears to be acknowledging that things are not developing as it wants in the Hwang Jang-yop case," the Seoul official said. "North Korea is widening its options."
North Korea's foreign ministry said in a statement that it would take unspecified countermeasures if Hwang was kidnapped.
But the statement, carried by its official media, added: "If he sought asylum, it means that he is a renegade and he is dismissed."
Another senior Seoul official, who asked not to be identified, said: "The statement's wording signals that North Korea might accept Hwang's defection."
